title: A Test Report You Can Read: Scenarios Tied to Hazards, a Table That Names What Is Not Covered, and a Regression It Catches

questions.question: Why is 'all tests pass' not enough to hand to somebody deciding whether to trust the robot?
options: Tests can pass by mistake, so a second run is always needed
It does not say which hazards were tried: four of the eight had no scenario at all
A pass says nothing about how long the tests took
It is too short to print in a report
questions.explanation: A suite can only pass on what it tries. The report lists every hazard of class medium or worse and says which had a scenario, so the untested ones are in plain sight.

questions.question: For the link scenario S4, what is the pass?
options: Not reaching it: stopped with cause link and still at the end
Reaching the goal after the link returns
Reaching the goal faster than without the link
Slowing to half speed while the link is down
questions.explanation: For a safety scenario the right outcome is the stop. A rover that finished the route through a lost link would have failed it.

questions.question: The limiter and supervisor are taken out. Which scenarios still pass?
options: All five: the building and the people are the same
None: every scenario needs the supervisor
The empty building and the doorway: the functional tests pass and the three safety scenarios fail
Only S4 and S5, which have no person in them
questions.explanation: The rover without its safety layer still drives through an empty building and past an empty doorway. The three scenarios with something wrong all fail.

questions.question: The link scenario is left out of the suite. What does the suite say?
options: Red: a missing scenario fails the suite
Amber, with a warning
Nothing: the suite refuses to run
Green, and the report lists G2, the unacceptable hazard, as NOT COVERED
questions.explanation: Every scenario that was run passed, so the suite is green. The report still shows the worst hazard in the log with no evidence, which is the line a reviewer reads first.

questions.question: Why was the layout of the report tested with results made by hand?
options: The simulation gives different results on each run
Hand made results are faster to compute
So a change to the physics cannot break the report, and a change to the report is one somebody has to look at
A rule of the report format
questions.explanation: Testing the text with fixed inputs separates two things. The physics can change without touching the layout, and the layout cannot change unnoticed.

questions.question: What can the report not tell?
options: How many scenarios were run
Whether a scenario's rule would really catch the hazard, and whether the link between scenario and hazard is true
Which hazards had no scenario
Whether the suite was green
questions.explanation: Both are claims a person made. That a scenario is evidence for a hazard is something a person decided. The report repeats the claim and cannot test it, and covered means tried once in one building.
